function: Soft MIMO detection for LDPC-coded systems: a trained autoencoder sets the sampling parameters of a path-sampling detector (TPbPS); Bayesian optimization tunes them for BLER (soft-TPbPS) (p. 2, 4-8).
system: 4x4 MIMO, 4 layers, LDPC-coded OFDM, 16/64/256-QAM, 2.15 GHz carrier, 15 kHz subcarrier spacing; no RIS (p. 8, Table II).
method: Autoencoder (fully connected encoder-decoder) trained supervised with cross-entropy and Adam on near-ML labels; Bayesian optimization with Gaussian-process surrogate tunes sampling parameters for BLER (p. 4-8).
data_channel: Link-level 5G NR simulator: AWGN and TDL-A (3GPP), TDL-D for generalization, Kronecker correlation; training on random QAM symbols through fading channels with AWGN (p. 5, 8-10).
test_conditions: Train: random QAM symbols over fading channels, imperfect CSI (p. 5, 8); test: TDL-A 3 km/h, AWGN, and TDL-D 60 km/h called a new environment (p. 8, 10).
baselines: LMMSE, FSD [3], [4], soft-FSD-SCA [10], IFSD [5], random sampling [14], near-optimum detector [24] (all non-learned); own variants TPbPS, TPbPS-SCA, soft-TPbPS-SCA (p. 9-10).
metrics: BER, BLER and SNR gain at 10% BLER, error probability vs SNR (diversity), run time per symbol, trainable parameters, training time and epochs (p. 9-11).
complexity: Measured run time per received symbol for 4x4, 64-QAM (Fig. 13); trainable parameters ~6k vs ~360k, training ~1 h vs >10 h (Table III) (p. 11).
openness: none (third-party BO library HEBO [29] used; no code or data of its own released)
q1_support: p. 8: "A link level simulator is developed to support 5G NR" and "time delay line (TDL) channel, is configured according to" the standard; Table II lists TDL-A and its footnote says the TDL models are defined in 3GPP.
q2_support: p. 10: "To illustrate the generalization performance of our proposed" method, BLER is given under "TDL-D fading channel model with speed of 60km/h", "when it is applied to a new" environment (main tests use TDL-A at 3 km/h, Table II).
q3_support: p. 9: "FSD [3] and TPbPS [1] are simulated for comparison" and "The BLER performance of LMMSE, FSD [4]" plus soft-FSD-SCA, near-optimum; p. 10: "IFSD in [5] and the original random sampling in [14]" are all non-learned; TPbPS is "our proposed TPbPS method" (p. 9), so no earlier learned detector is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the respect to the run time in Fig. 13" gives the measured run time per received symbol of all detectors; p. 11: "number of real-valued trainable neural network" parameters is reported in Table III (about 6k vs 360k).
q5_support: p. 8: "A link level simulator is developed to support 5G NR" is the authors' own simulator; p. 9: "we utilize the Bayesian optimization library developed" by a third party [29]; no code, data or link of the paper itself is given.
notes: Included, area 1: soft MIMO detection, 4x4 LDPC-coded. q1=1: the simulator uses the 3GPP TDL-A/TDL-D profiles (Table II footnote 2 on p. 8), but the standard cited for the channel, [28], is TS 38.212 (coding) and TR 38.901 is not cited; training channel is only called fading channels (p. 5), reviewer to confirm. q2=1 rests on the TDL-D 60 km/h test called a new environment (p. 10); the training channel is not stated explicitly, reviewer to confirm. q3=0: all baselines are non-learned and TPbPS [1] is the authors' preliminary version of their own proposed TPbPS (footnote 1, p. 2; p. 9), so I did not count it as an earlier learned baseline; the reviewer may flip q3 if it is counted as an earlier paper of the same authors.
